summary.title: Clouds Against Humanity: pipeline data flow diagram
summary.description: Teaching model for the Threat Dragon exercise. Trust boundaries B1 to B8 match docs/wiki/Threat-Model-Exercise.md; T-numbers match docs/wiki/Threat-Model.md. A model records what someone believes; it does not verify the system. Generic names only. Audited against the repository code on 2026-10-24 (see docs/threat-model/README.md): a threat is Mitigated only when a control is visible in code or config, and anything that cannot be confirmed from the repository starts with UNVERIFIED.

diagrams.title: Contributor to protected resource
diagrams.description: Contributor and maintainer through the repository, CI, Spacelift, Doppler and the cloud API to the connector droplets and Twingate.

data.name: Internet scanner (A1)
data.description: A1: an anonymous party on the internet with no account. Scans for open ports and exposed services.

threats.title: Scanner pretends to be a legitimate client
threats.description: T1: an anonymous party tries to talk to a connector as if it were a client.
threats.mitigation: Zero public inbound rules. modules/firewall/main.tf emits inbound rules only from the firewall's own tag or one other group's tag, never an address; stacks/10-access/main.tf passes only connector-tag TCP 22 (plus metrics ports from a telemetry tag, empty by default). .spacelift/policies/plan.rego denies any non-tag inbound rule at plan time (UNVERIFIED: that this policy is attached in Spacelift). scripts/zero_ports_check.py is an external check run by hand, from one vantage point at one moment. Connectors dial out only.

data.name: Contributor (A2)
data.description: Full name: Contributor or fork author (A2). A2: someone who can propose code through a pull request but cannot push or merge.

threats.title: Pull request made to look like a trusted change
threats.description: T3: a pull request edits a security-critical file (the secrets hook) alongside a harmless-looking test change.
threats.mitigation: Reading the changed-file list is a human step, not a control in the repository. Verified limits on the damage: .spacelift/policies/push.rego never proposes a run, scripts/spacelift/doppler-env.sh fetches secrets only for a tracked or destroy run on main, and .github/workflows/ci.yml gives CI no cloud credential. UNVERIFIED: branch protection and a required CI green check on main (GitHub settings, not readable from a clone). Open until the merge gate is checked in the repository settings.

threats.title: No proof of who confirmed or authored a change beyond repository history
threats.description: No T-number: repudiation is the weakest letter in Threat-Model.md. History shows authors; nothing in the repository proves who pressed confirm in Spacelift.
threats.mitigation: Open gap. Candidate control: review the Spacelift audit trail (verify in the vendor console).

data.name: Upstream publishers
data.description: Full name: Upstream publishers (actions, Doppler CLI, apt repos). Supply chain: the publishers of pinned CI actions, the Doppler CLI release, the Twingate apt repository and Ubuntu mirrors.

threats.title: Tampered download or action
threats.description: T7, T8, T9: a compromised action, CLI binary or package is pulled into the pipeline or onto a droplet. Evidence: ci.yml and wiki.yml pin each reusable workflow by full commit SHA; scripts/spacelift/doppler-env.sh pins the Doppler CLI by SHA-256; modules/twingate-bootstrap/cloud-init.yaml.tftpl pins the Twingate apt key by fingerprint and refuses any extra key in the file (cah-apt-key-check, see the tampered Twingate package threat).
threats.mitigation: Workflow references pinned by commit SHA (ci.yml, wiki.yml); Doppler CLI pinned by SHA-256 per architecture and fail closed (doppler-env.sh, cah_doppler_install). The Twingate apt key pin is now strict (cah-apt-key-check refuses extra keys; see the tampered Twingate package threat, Mitigated). The umbrella stays Open for the other causes: the unpinned weekly connector package update, ci.yml's unpinned pytest install, and a pinned commit that was already malicious. Residual: a pinned commit that was already malicious; ci.yml installs pytest unpinned.

data.name: Maintainer (A3/A4)
data.description: Full name: Maintainer and laptop (A3 / A4). A3: whoever can push to main (one writer today). A4: a stolen maintainer identity (Twingate sign-in plus SSH key). Holds the Twingate client and the SSH key.

threats.title: Maintainer identity or session stolen
threats.description: T2: stolen Twingate credentials. Together with the SSH key this gives a shell on a connector. The exercise notes there is no numbered threat for takeover of the maintainer's own accounts.
threats.mitigation: Sign-in delegated to the identity provider (enforce MFA there; not visible in this repository); SSH key still required. Verify account hardening in each vendor console.

threats.title: Anyone who can push to main is trusted
threats.description: T3: the design assumes one writer. A second writer, or a taken-over writer account, makes pull request and tracked-run attacks real.
threats.mitigation: Branch protection, one writer, required reviews before adding a second writer. Settings live outside the repository: verify by hand.

data.name: Source repo
data.description: Full name: Source repository and main branch. Public repository. UNVERIFIED: branch protection on main and a required CI green check are GitHub settings, not readable from a clone (the job named CI green exists in .github/workflows/ci.yml). Holds code and the pipeline definition. Holds no cloud credential.

threats.title: Malicious change to the secrets hook or .spacelift/config.yml
threats.description: T3: a change makes the hook print the Doppler token. Every automated check can pass a few changed lines.
threats.mitigation: Verifiable controls only narrow the harm: push.rego never proposes a run (UNVERIFIED: that it is attached in Spacelift), doppler-env.sh skips secrets unless the run is tracked on main, and ci.yml holds no cloud credential. Nothing in the repository stops a reviewed and merged change to the hook, which then runs on main next to DOPPLER_TOKEN; docs/spacelift-secrets.md section 8 says the script's checks only guard honest code. What is left is a person reading the diff and UNVERIFIED branch protection.

threats.title: Operator identifiers leak through the public repository
threats.description: T14: account ids, address ranges, names or machine identifiers end up in a commit, doc or issue.
threats.mitigation: Identifiers live in Doppler (docs/spacelift-secrets.md section 2). modules/twingate-bootstrap/main.tf drops the SSH key comment before it reaches cloud-init. scripts/identifier_check.py runs in the python job of ci.yml, and gitleaks runs in the pinned security workflow (on by default; ci.yml does not turn it off). Residual: human error in a commit message or doc, and anything the checks have no pattern for.

threats.title: Branch protection is a setting, not a file
threats.description: No T-number. If branch protection is switched off, nothing in the diff shows it.
threats.mitigation: Verify the setting by hand in the repository settings; it cannot be checked from a clone.

data.name: CI (GitHub Actions)
data.description: Runs pytest, the cost gate and tofu test on pull request code. permissions: {} by default; no cloud credential.

threats.title: Hostile test prints a secret
threats.description: T3, T7: a pull request's code runs in CI and tries to read or print a secret. Evidence: ci.yml sets permissions to an empty block at the top level and grants contents: read per job; it passes no secret and no Doppler input to the reusable workflows.
threats.mitigation: CI holds no cloud credential: ci.yml passes no secrets and no Doppler inputs. The reusable python and tofu workflows keep id-token out of the jobs that run repository code (read in their source at the pinned commit). Worst case is wasted minutes.

threats.title: Compromised action runs in CI
threats.description: T7: a pinned action is malicious or its pin is moved.
threats.mitigation: Every action pinned by commit SHA; permissions: {} by default. Residual: a compromised pinned commit is trusted until the pin changes.

data.name: Spacelift proposed run
data.description: Full name: Spacelift proposed run (pull request). A plan-only run. The push policy never proposes one, so no pull request code should run here. If one does start, the cah-doppler context is attached to every run type and exposes DOPPLER_TOKEN to it; only the unmodified hook skips fetching the named secrets (docs/spacelift-secrets.md, section 8).

threats.title: A pull request becomes a run next to the secrets
threats.description: T3: until the push policy is attached in Spacelift, a same-repository pull request that changes a stack still gets a proposed run, and the hook script is read from the pull request's branch.
threats.mitigation: UNVERIFIED (a Spacelift setting): whether .spacelift/policies/push.rego is attached. The repository keeps and tests the file (push_test.rego, run by the policy job of ci.yml). Attach it in Spacelift (paid plan) or narrow project roots and globs (free plan); nobody else opens pull requests until then. Verify in the console.

data.name: Spacelift tracked run
data.description: Full name: Spacelift tracked run (main). Runs plan and apply for a stack from main. Holds DOPPLER_TOKEN and the per-stack secrets loaded in before_init. Apply waits for a human confirm (a Spacelift stack setting, UNVERIFIED from the repository; .spacelift/policies/plan.rego denies a plan from a stack with autodeploy on).

threats.title: A compromised tracked run reaches every prd secret
threats.description: T3, T4, T10: code that executes during init or plan runs before the confirm gate, with DOPPLER_TOKEN scoped to the whole prd config. The per-stack secret list is not isolation.
threats.mitigation: Gates before main: pull request, CI green, branch protection (UNVERIFIED setting), one writer. The confirm gate reviews the plan; it does not stop code that already ran. .spacelift/policies/plan.rego checks the plan's resource changes, not code that executed during init or plan.

threats.title: Apply of a plan nobody reviewed
threats.description: T11: autodeploy applies a bad plan.
threats.mitigation: A person confirms every apply. .spacelift/policies/plan.rego denies any plan from a stack with autodeploy on (covered by plan_test.rego; UNVERIFIED: that the plan policy is attached). scripts/cost_check.py and scripts/ci_cost_gate.sh run in the python job of ci.yml against docs/stages/approved.json.

threats.title: Resources outside the repository run up the bill
threats.description: T11: spend from resources created outside the repository or bandwidth overage is not covered by the cost gate.
threats.mitigation: Billing alerts at $10 and $25 are stated in docs/wiki/Threat-Model.md and cannot be confirmed from the repository (UNVERIFIED). The cost gate sees only resources the repository declares. Residual: check the cloud account for undeclared resources.

data.name: OpenTofu state
data.description: Full name: OpenTofu state in Spacelift. State holds connector tokens and the full resource map. Stored only in Spacelift (the stacks declare no backend block; UNVERIFIED from the repository).

threats.title: Connector token read out of state
threats.description: T6: anyone who can read stack state sees the connector tokens.
threats.mitigation: The user_data output is marked sensitive (modules/twingate-bootstrap/outputs.tf). The stacks declare no backend block, so state is Spacelift-managed (UNVERIFIED: state access settings are not readable from the repository). Accepted: restrict state access in Spacelift.

data.name: Doppler prd config
data.description: Every runtime secret: cloud token, Twingate API token, tenant name, admin key name and user ids. Read through a read-only, single-config service token (docs/spacelift-secrets.md; a vendor setting, UNVERIFIED from the repository). .spacelift/config.yml loads names for stacks 00, 10 and 20.

threats.title: Doppler service token leaks
threats.description: T4: the service token reads all prd secrets until revoked. Nothing records who read the config.
threats.mitigation: Documented setup (docs/spacelift-secrets.md sections 2 and 4): read-only, one config, 90-day expiry, write-only in the Spacelift context. These are Doppler and Spacelift settings, UNVERIFIED from the repository. The same token also serves the telemetry stack (.spacelift/config.yml, cah-20-telemetry). Rotate every value it could read, not only the token.

threats.title: Vendor compromise or outage
threats.description: T10: a hosted control plane is compromised or unavailable.
threats.mitigation: Accepted: inherent to using hosted control planes.

data.name: Cloud provider API
data.description: The provider API that creates droplets and firewalls. Reached with a write-scoped token (custom scopes listed in docs/spacelift-secrets.md section 4a: project, vpc, firewall, tag, droplet, ssh_key read).

threats.title: Runaway bill through the provider API
threats.description: T11: an unreviewed or malicious apply creates expensive resources.
threats.mitigation: scripts/cost_check.py allows only approved resource types and totals (docs/stages/approved.json) and runs in ci.yml. plan.rego denies world-open inbound rules and protected deletes, not cost. Billing alerts at $10 and $25 are UNVERIFIED.

threats.title: Write token can open anything in the account
threats.description: T10: a stolen write token can create, destroy or open anything in the account.
threats.mitigation: Custom scopes (docs/spacelift-secrets.md section 4a): project, vpc, firewall, tag and droplet with create, read, update and delete; ssh_key read; image, region, size and actions read. That is wider than droplets, firewalls and tags: it includes the project and the VPC. plan.rego denies a plan that deletes or replaces a VPC, project or firewall (UNVERIFIED: attached). The token sits in Doppler and is loaded only on tracked or destroy runs from main. Accepted vendor trust.

data.name: Twingate
data.description: Full name: Twingate controller and relay. Hosted zero-trust control plane. Signs the maintainer in through the identity provider and enforces per-resource access.

threats.title: Stolen Twingate credentials
threats.description: T2: an attacker presents the maintainer's identity to Twingate.
threats.mitigation: Verified in code: stacks/10-access/main.tf defines two Twingate resources, TCP 22 only, UDP denied, ICMP off, granted to one admin group; cloud-init sshd hardening allows only cah-admin with a key and no password. UNVERIFIED: MFA at the identity provider and the Twingate sign-in policy (vendor settings). Open until those are checked in each console.

threats.title: Vendor compromise
threats.description: T10: the control plane is compromised.
threats.mitigation: Narrow scopes; end-to-end encryption to connectors; separate SSH key gate. Accepted.

data.name: Connector droplets
data.description: Full name: Connector droplets (two). Two outbound-only connector droplets. No public inbound rules. Outbound is open to any address on TCP 443, 80 and 53, UDP 53 and 123, TCP 30000 to 31000 and all UDP ports (modules/firewall/main.tf, stacks/10-access/main.tf); there is no outbound allowlist. Hold their connector token in a root-only file.

threats.title: Connector token readable via the metadata endpoint
threats.description: T5: user-data is readable by any local process through the metadata endpoint.
threats.mitigation: Token file is root-only 0600 (connector.conf in the cloud-init template). An opt-in lock exists: metadata_lock in modules/twingate-bootstrap limits the metadata endpoint to root and the monitoring agent user, but it defaults to false and its variable text says it is not tested on a real machine, so by default any local process can read user-data. AWS connectors require IMDSv2 with a hop limit of 1 (modules/aws/twingate-connector/main.tf), which does not stop a local process. Accepted until the lock is rolled out.

threats.title: Both connectors down, operator locked out
threats.description: T13: no console password by design.
threats.mitigation: Two connectors with staggered reboots and updates (reboot_times in stacks/10-access, weekly update 30 minutes after the reboot time in modules/twingate-bootstrap/main.tf). Accepted: no console password by design (lock_passwd in cloud-init); recovery is a rebuild through Spacelift.

threats.title: Lateral movement between droplets
threats.description: T12: a compromised droplet moves to another. Evidence: the connector firewall allows TCP 22 between members of the connector tag in both directions (stacks/10-access/main.tf), because Twingate may route a session to either connector.
threats.mitigation: Cloud firewall: inbound only from the connector tag on TCP 22, same-tag outbound on 22, no address rules (modules/firewall/main.tf, tests/firewall.tftest.hcl); sshd allows only cah-admin with a key. The connector-to-connector SSH path is allowed on purpose, so this narrows lateral movement to SSH between the two; it does not remove it.

threats.title: Exposed service exploited from the internet
threats.description: T1: scanning, brute force or exploit of an exposed service.
threats.mitigation: Zero public inbound rules attached by tag at creation (see the scanner threat), plus sshd hardening in cloud-init: no root login, no passwords, AllowUsers cah-admin, MaxAuthTries 3. Unattended security upgrades are on. The host firewall (host_firewall) is an opt-in second layer, default false and untested on a real machine.

data.name: Protected resources
data.description: Full name: Protected resources (SSH on a private host). What Twingate exposes: one host and one port per resource (TCP 22). Placeholder for whatever later sits behind a connector.

threats.title: Identity plus SSH key together give a shell
threats.description: T2: an attacker with both the identity and the SSH key gets a shell. Stage 2 would make this a foothold with a path home.
threats.mitigation: One host and port per resource; sshd allows only the admin user with a key. Stage 2 needs its own Twingate group and service account.

data.name: Blocked inbound traffic
data.description: Full label: Unsolicited inbound traffic (blocked). Port scans and connection attempts from the internet. Nothing is listening: no inbound rules.

threats.title: Flood or brute force against a connector
threats.description: T1: unsolicited traffic aimed at the droplets.
threats.mitigation: Zero public inbound rules (modules/firewall/main.tf; plan.rego denies non-tag inbound); connectors are outbound-only.

data.name: Fork pull request
data.description: Full label: Fork pull request (code, no secrets). Proposed code. No credentials cross this flow in either direction.

threats.title: Pull request edits the pipeline
threats.description: T3: the pull request changes scripts, workflows or stack definitions.
threats.mitigation: CI only for a pull request: ci.yml holds no credential, and push.rego proposes no Spacelift run (UNVERIFIED: attached; see the proposed-run threat). Review of the changed-file list is a human step.

data.name: PR code checkout
data.description: Full label: Pull request code checkout (code). CI checks out the pull request code and runs repository code on it.

threats.title: Pull request code runs with CI permissions
threats.description: T3, T7: hostile repository code runs in CI.
threats.mitigation: ci.yml: permissions empty at the top level, contents: read per job, no secrets passed. The reusable workflows keep id-token out of jobs that run repository code (read at the pinned commit).

data.name: CI status check
data.description: Full label: CI green status check (build result). The CI result that branch protection requires before merge.

data.name: Action refs by SHA
data.description: Full label: Action refs resolved by commit SHA (code). Third-party action code fetched at a pinned commit.

threats.title: Action pin moved to malicious code
threats.description: T7: the pinned reference changes or the pinned commit was already malicious.
threats.mitigation: Every reusable workflow reference in ci.yml and wiki.yml is a full commit SHA; changing the pin is a reviewed diff. Residual: a pin that was already malicious.

data.name: Review and merge
data.description: Full label: Review and merge (approval, code). The maintainer reviews the diff and merges to main. The only path to a tracked run.

threats.title: Merge authorship rests on repository history only
threats.description: No T-number: the repository records the merge, not whether branch protection was on at the time.
threats.mitigation: Verify branch protection settings by hand; review audit logs in the vendor console.

data.name: PR push event
data.description: Full label: Pull request push event (commit ref; policy decides). Webhook telling Spacelift about a pull request branch. The push policy should answer: never propose.

threats.title: Policy missing: pull request starts a proposed run
threats.description: T3: without the push policy attached, a same-repository pull request gets a proposed run. A fork starts nothing unless a policy defines allow_fork.
threats.mitigation: UNVERIFIED (a Spacelift setting): attach .spacelift/policies/push.rego. The repository keeps and tests it (push_test.rego, policy job in ci.yml); Spacelift does not read it from the repository.

data.name: Merged commit
data.description: Full label: Merged commit on main (code). The commit a tracked run will plan and apply.

threats.title: Malicious change merged to main
threats.description: T3: anyone who can push to main is trusted.
threats.mitigation: Accepted: pull request, CI green, branch protection, one writer.

data.name: Doppler CLI download
data.description: Full label: Doppler CLI download (binary). The pinned Doppler CLI release fetched by the secrets hook.

threats.title: Tampered Doppler CLI
threats.description: T8: a modified binary runs next to the secrets.
threats.mitigation: Pinned version and SHA-256 per architecture; a mismatch deletes the file and stops the run (scripts/spacelift/doppler-env.sh, cah_doppler_install; tests/test_doppler_env.py).

data.name: Service token read
data.description: Full label: Read request with service token (DOPPLER_TOKEN). The run presents the read-only service token and asks for secrets by name.

threats.title: Service token appears in a log
threats.description: T4: the token or a fetched value is printed in a run log.
threats.mitigation: Each fetched value is passed to ::add-mask (doppler-env.sh). docs/spacelift-secrets.md section 8 says masking is not confirmed on a real run and that the mask line itself may appear in the log. UNVERIFIED. Open until the first tracked run's log is searched for the token prefix.

threats.title: Stolen service token used to ask Doppler for secrets
threats.description: T4: Doppler decides who is asking by one token, so whoever holds it is treated as the run.
threats.mitigation: Read-only, one config and 90-day expiry are documented (docs/spacelift-secrets.md sections 2 and 4) and are vendor settings, UNVERIFIED from the repository. Revoke on suspicion.

data.name: Secrets returned
data.description: Full label: Secrets (cloud token, Twingate API token, tenant, admin key). Secret values returned to the run and loaded into the environment before the plan.

threats.title: Secrets read in transit or by run code
threats.description: T4: any code that executes in the run can read the environment.
threats.mitigation: TLS to Doppler; values are masked (UNVERIFIED, see the service-token log threat). doppler-env.sh exports every fetched value into the run's environment before the plan, so any code in init or plan can read it. Gates before main.

data.name: State and tokens
data.description: Full label: OpenTofu state (connector tokens, resource map). State written and read by the run.

threats.title: State readable by anyone with stack access
threats.description: T6: connector tokens sit in state.
threats.mitigation: Marked sensitive; restrict state access in Spacelift. Accepted.

data.name: Plan for review
data.description: Full label: Plan for review (resource changes). The plan a human reads before confirming.

data.name: Human confirms apply
data.description: Full label: Confirm apply (human approval). The single human gate between plan and apply.

threats.title: Nothing in the repository proves who pressed confirm
threats.description: No T-number: the model's weakest letter.
threats.mitigation: Open. Review the Spacelift audit trail; verify in the console.

data.name: Apply with cloud token
data.description: Full label: Apply: create or destroy droplets and firewalls (cloud token). Provider API calls made with the write-scoped token after confirm.

threats.title: Plan differs from what the code would do
threats.description: T3, T11: code that ran during plan calls the provider directly, before any confirm.
threats.mitigation: plan.rego inspects the plan's resource changes (non-tag inbound rules, IPv6, protected deletes, autodeploy), which limits what an honest plan may contain. It cannot see code that already ran during init or plan, the same gap as the compromised tracked run threat. UNVERIFIED: that the plan policy is attached.

data.name: Create droplet
data.description: Full label: Droplet create with user-data (connector token). Cloud-init carries the connector token to the droplet.

threats.title: Token in user-data
threats.description: T5, T6: the connector token travels in user-data and sits in state.
threats.mitigation: Root-only file; revocable per connector; metadata_lock exists but is off by default (see the metadata endpoint threat). Accepted.

data.name: Twingate API call
data.description: Full label: Twingate API: resources, connectors, tokens (API token). The run uses the Read, Write and Provision key to create connectors and issue tokens.

threats.title: Stolen API key creates its own connector
threats.description: T4: whoever holds the Twingate key can create a connector or issue tokens for an existing one.
threats.mitigation: After a leak, rotate the key and look in the console for connectors the code does not declare. .spacelift/config.yml loads the same TWINGATE_API_TOKEN for stacks 10 and 20, so its reach is the tenant, not one stack (docs/spacelift-secrets.md section 2 lists only stack 10).

data.name: IdP sign-in
data.description: Full label: IdP sign-in and resource request (identity). The maintainer signs in through the identity provider and requests one resource.

threats.title: Identity replayed or phished
threats.description: T2: stolen credentials or session.
threats.mitigation: Per-resource ACL and key-only sshd are verified in code (see the stolen Twingate credentials threat). UNVERIFIED: MFA at the identity provider. Open until checked.

data.name: Outbound connector link
data.description: Full label: Outbound connector link (connector token). The connector dials out to Twingate and presents its token. Nothing dials in to the droplet.

threats.title: Stolen connector token used to impersonate a connector
threats.description: T5: a token taken from the droplet or state is presented elsewhere.
threats.mitigation: One twingate_connector and one token pair per connector (modules/twingate-bootstrap/main.tf). Revocation is a Twingate console action, UNVERIFIED from the repository; nothing in the repository detects a second connector presenting a stolen token.

data.name: Relayed session
data.description: Full label: Relayed session (user traffic). Authorized user traffic, carried to the connector over the link the connector opened. One direction in the diagram: Twingate to the droplet.

data.name: SSH to resource
data.description: Full label: SSH to the protected resource (TCP 22, key required). The only traffic Twingate admits.

threats.title: Move from one droplet to another
threats.description: T12: lateral movement. Evidence: see the lateral-movement threat on the connector droplets; the path between the two connectors is allowed on purpose.
threats.mitigation: Firewall admits only connector-tagged SSH between the two droplets (stacks/10-access/main.tf) and sshd allows only cah-admin with a key. The path exists by design; this narrows it, it does not remove it.

data.name: Signed apt packages
data.description: Full label: Signed packages (apt repo, pinned key). Twingate and Ubuntu packages installed at first boot.

threats.title: Tampered Twingate package
threats.description: T9: a modified package installs on a connector. Finding (fixed, issue 288): the cloud-init check used to be a grep for the pinned fingerprint, so a key file holding the pinned key plus another key passed and the whole file was dearmored into the apt keyring. The connector install now calls /usr/local/sbin/cah-apt-key-check, the same strict helper the Wazuh agent install uses, which refuses any file that is not exactly one primary key with the pinned fingerprint.
threats.mitigation: The pinned key file must be exactly one key: modules/twingate-bootstrap/cloud-init.yaml.tftpl calls cah-apt-key-check before gpg --dearmor, and apt verifies package signatures against that keyring (signed-by). Tests: tests/test_log_shipping_hardening.py (test_twingate_install_refuses_the_pinned_key_plus_an_extra_key, test_twingate_install_refuses_a_stray_extra_fingerprint_record, test_the_twingate_install_block_uses_the_strict_key_check_not_a_grep). Residual: Twingate's own signing key, and a weekly unpinned apt-get install of the connector package (cron.d/twingate-connector-update).

data.name: B1: no inbound
data.description: Nothing from the internet may reach a connector droplet. Zero public inbound rules.

data.name: B2: PR, CI only
data.description: A stranger's pull request reaches the repository and CI only, with no credentials.

label.text: B3: push policy never proposes a Spacelift run

data.name: B3: push policy never proposes a Spacelift run
data.description: Pull request code must not start a Spacelift run. The policy lives in Spacelift, not in the repository.

data.name: B4: branch protection + CI green
data.description: The only path to main. Branch protection is a setting outside the repository.

data.name: B5: tracked run on main
data.description: Only a merged commit on main becomes a tracked run.

label.text: B6: read-only token, fetched by name

data.name: B6: read-only token, fetched by name
data.description: Doppler to Spacelift: read-only service token scoped to the one prd config.
